newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First attacks Bolger for "bad mouthing" economy.
newsitem.headline: NZ First attacks Bolger for "bad mouthing" economy.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Monday attacked Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Telecom Corp chairman Peter Shirtcliffe for "bad mouthing" the New Zealand economy to Australian audiences.

Earlier in the election campaign, Shirtcliffe warned Australians their $20 billion in investments in New Zealand could be at risk if populist politicians implemented their policies -- a clear reference to economic nationalist New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance.

Bolger, in an Australian television interview on Sunday, said if he was an overseas investor he would wait until after the October 12 election to make sure a "sensible coalition" emerged. He said investor uncertainty over New Zealand was "totally understandable" just two weeks from the poll.

Peters told a public meeting in Wellington that Bolger had "appeared on television and began to bad mouth the New Zealand economy when he said to Australian investors in short if the other side gets in then you had better get your investments out of this country because there willl be a disaster'".
"How many people in other democracies would tolerate a PM making that sort of statement?"
In response to an interjector Peters said: "It's political treason, you're right, and could be economic treason were it not for the fact the Aussies are not as dumb as Jim Bolger.

"He is behaving like a spoilt brat. He is saying: I have to be Prime Minister or things will be disastrous'. Well, people are saying 'they are disastrous now and we don't want you to be Prime Minister'."

He alleged a clique in the governing National Party was preparing to replace Bolger after the election. Peters has not ruled out forming a coalition with National after the election provided Bolger and his finance minister Bill Birch are dumped.
Peters said Shirtcliffe and Bolger were scared of democracy.
"Shirtcliffe is afraid his multi-national, owned abroad, may not be able to go on profit-gouging New Zealand people."

He added: "New Zealand business people and business people abroad have no reason to fear New Zealand First - except for some of the hot money merchants and the wide boys, who are here today and gone tomorrow.
"When someone like Jim Bolger says investors will flee. they demonstate just how little they understand about the financial markets of any country.
"You can't pack your tent and flee in the night if you are an international investor from abroad. Somebody has got to buy the tent, otherwise you flee with nothing," Peters said.
New Zealand First is averaging 16.7 percent in the polls, down from a high of 30 percent earlier this year.

On current polling New Zealand First, the Alliance and the main opposition Labour Party could together oust the ruling National Party, but it is still unclear if they will be able to strike a coalition deal.

Commenting on other parties' fiscal policy, Peters said National was promising extra spending of $1.4 billion, and NZ First $1.64 billion. "Labour's is frankly off the wall. It can't be costed and that is the grave danger in this campaign. And the Alliance is spending far more than that.
"We are campaigning...on a thoroughly respectable...orthodox policy that places its total focus on exporting to expand the wealth of this country."
